title: Malus's law through two polarisers
caption: The first polariser passes half of unpolarised light. The second passes cos²θ of what reaches it, so at 60° the final intensity is ½ × cos² 60° = 0.125 I₀: one eighth.
alt: Final intensity as a fraction of the original against the angle between the polarisers, falling from 0.5 at 0 degrees to 0.125 at 60 degrees and zero at 90.
description: After the first polariser: ½I₀, whatever its orientation.
After the second, at angle θ: ½I₀ cos²θ.
At 90° (crossed polarisers) no light gets through.

checks.name: half the light passes when aligned
